transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-30 10:00 PT
Duration: 58 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Alejandro Ruiz (Redwood SE), Priya Malhotra (NexusTech Head of Platform), Samir Patel (NexusTech ML Eng), Lola Jefferson (NexusTech Infra)
Recording ID: nt-meet-20261130-01

Summary:
- Goal: define POC success criteria for NexusTech real-time assistant workload; agree on traffic profile (QPS, concurrency, token distribution), benchmarks, and timeline.
- Key asks from customer: predictable p99/p95 latency under burst, data residency and KMS controls, and cost targets.
- Proposed POC: 3 week run (capture, baseline replay, tuning) with synthetic and live-replay benchmarks.

Topics: workload capture, QPS and burst modeling, token mix (input/output), concurrency, SLOs, security checks, timeline and deliverables.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): great morning everyone, thanks for carving out time, uh quick intro from our side, I'm Maya, AE on the account, and Ale, our systems SE, is with me.
[00:12] Alejandro (Redwood SE): hey all, hola. I run perf and infra for these POCs, so I'll lead the benchmark design.
[00:20] Priya (NexusTech): thanks, Maya. On our side Priya, I'll kick off with context: we're building an in-app assistant across three products, mostly real-time chat and short form completions. Main ask is we want to validate that we can hit latency SLOs during sales peaks and events.
[00:35] Samir (NexusTech): yeah hi, Samir here. quick numbers: today baseline QPS is low but our projected peak for GA is roughly 1,200 QPS, with bursts up to ~6k QPS for short windows. Concurrency is tricky, because many requests are streaming.
[00:50] Lola (NexusTech): infra note: we need VPC and customer-managed KMS; any proposal without KMS is non-starter for us.
[00:58] Maya: noted. ok, high level we typically run a three-phase POC: 1) traffic capture + config, 2) baseline replay and characterize tails, 3) tuning + report + recommendation. timeline usually 2-4 weeks depending on data.
[01:16] Priya: 3 weeks ideal, shorter preferred. what do you need for the capture?
[01:22] Alejandro: we need 48 hours of sampled requests — headers removed — plus distribution on input and output token lengths. If you can't share raw, we can give a small capture tool that anonymizes - it's a script that outputs per-request token count and timestamps.
[01:38] Samir: fine, we can do that. our avg user prompt is about 28 tokens, median output about 72 tokens, but during help flows output can go up to 420 tokens occasionally.
[01:49] Maya: good, that token skew matters a lot for batching and KV cache. For sizing we model three buckets: short (<64 out), medium (64-256), long (>256). Do those categories map to your traffic?
[02:05] Samir: roughly yes, about 65% short, 28% medium, 7% long.
[02:12] Alejandro: ok that distribution is very helpful. now on QPS: you said projected peak 1.2k and bursts to 6k. Is that sustained for minutes or seconds?
[02:22] Priya: short spikes, usually 1-3 minutes during marketing pushes, but sometimes up to 10 minutes during large launches.
[02:30] Lola: and we have regional fans in EU, so we'd want multi-region fallback.
[02:36] Maya: that's doable. For the POC we'll map to a single region first, but include a failover plan. We should define SLOs: what are you targeting for p95 and p99 generation latency?
[02:47] Priya: p95 under 350ms would be great, p99 under 900ms. If that's unrealistic we're flexible, but we need clear tradeoffs vs cost.
[02:58] Alejandro: ok for the model class you mentioned (we discussed using an Llama-ish open model), hitting p95 350ms at 1.2k QPS is challenging on hosted small nodes — this is where Redwood Dedicatd options help. Also batching and prefix caching shift latencies.
[03:15] Samir: can you quantify? like cost per 1M tokens or number of GPUs?
[03:20] Alejandro: rough ballpark: for a 7B/13B family model with quantization, to meet that latency SLO at 1.2k sustained QPS you'd want a Dedicated pool of 8-12 A100-class GPUs with affinity for streaming. For hosted we might need autoscale and relaxed SLOs or smaller model. Cost per 1M tokens will vary but we'll sketch numbers in the pricing doc.
[03:41] Priya: hmm 8-12 GPUs is heavier than we expected. are there alternatives — model distillation, quant, or batching tradeoffs?
[03:48] Alejandro: yes: 1) lower model size or use a distilled variant — drop latency but may affect quality; 2) enable continuous KV caching for repeated context to reduce compute per token; 3) longer batching windows reduce cost but increase tail. We can surface tradeoff curves in the POC.
[04:03] Maya: we'll show you a workload cost vs latency chart. For the POC benchmarks we run both "replay" (your captured traffic played back at scale) and a synthetic stress test for tails (step increases to 6k+ QPS). We'll capture p50/p95/p99 and CPU/GPU utilization, queue depths, and token throughput.
[04:20] Priya: replay is very important; synthetic alone won't show the chat patterns.
[04:24] Alejandro: agreed. replay helps us validate KV cache hit patterns as well. Also, we need to instrument token mix — input vs output. If your UI streams tokens, we need to test streaming vs non-streaming latencies.
[04:38] Samir: our clients mostly stream — about 70% of calls use streaming.
[04:42] Maya: ok we'll include streaming scenarios. Regarding security, Lola, you asked for KMS and SSO — we support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments and can integrate SAML SSO for console access. We'll attach SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
[04:56] Lola: we also want audit logs and per-customer RBAC. Is that available in Dedicated?
[05:02] Alejandro: yes Dedicated and Private come with audit log retention and RBAC; hosted has standard logs but we can discuss retention add-ons.
[05:10] Priya: what exact telemetry do you need for the capture script?
[05:14] Alejandro: timestamp, anonymized request id, input token count, output token count (if available), stream flag, and a minimal intent tag if you can extract (like "search", "assistant", "summarize"). If you can't, just token counts are fine.
[05:28] Samir: we can strip user content and produce a sanitized csv. will do.
[05:33] Maya: perfect. Next, bench specifics: we'll run 3 baseline suites:
 - Baseline replay at projected GA (1.2k QPS) for 30m.
 - Burst test ladder: ramp to 6k QPS in steps (1.2k, 2.4k, 4k, 6k) holding at each for 2-5m.
 - Long tail endurance: 12 hour run at 20% of peak to check memory leak / KV churn.
[06:00] Priya: that sounds good. how do we interpret failures? example: if p99 goes to 1.5s under 6k burst, is that acceptable?
[06:09] Alejandro: we'll map against your SLOs. POC success criteria we propose: 1) under normal projected peak (1.2k) p95 <= 450ms and p99 <= 900ms; 2) under 6k short burst p95 <= 750ms and p99 <= 1.6s; 3) no more than 5% error rate or timeouts; 4) quantifiable unit cost within target range (we'll put a tentative $/1M token).
[06:34] Priya: ok that gives us a starting point. We'd like p95 350ms if possible but we'll take your proposed numbers.
[06:40] Lola: about data residency — we need EU data to stay in EU region. Will the POC restrict region?
[06:46] Maya: yes we can run the POC in eu-west, mirror the infra. For dedicated we can provision in region. We'll include a fall-back plan to reroute to other regions if capacity is exceeded.
[06:58] Priya: can you run comparisons: Hosted vs Dedicated cost and latency?
[07:03] Alejandro: yes, baseline will include two configurations: Hosted (autoscale, multi-tenant but cheaper) and Dedicated (reserved GPU pool, better tail latency). We'll capture the same workloads and compare.
[07:13] Samir: for streaming requests — how do you model concurrency?
[07:17] Alejandro: we look at concurrent open websocket sessions and avg token emission rate. For streaming heavy usage, the concurrency metric becomes sessions * average window size. We'll simulate this with our streaming harness (we use a patched wrk + streaming shim).
[07:30] Maya: another thing: warm vs cold starts. If users are new, KV cache misses can blow up token compute. We'll simulate cold starts during the ladder test.
[07:40] Priya: good note. Also need to validate model fallbacks in case of overload: auto-fallback to a smaller model. Can Redwood route by policy?
[07:49] Alejandro: yes smart routing — we can set policies by latency and cost threshold to route to cheaper model variants during overload. We'll test that as part of the POC.
[07:59] Priya: who will run the replay? us or Redwood?
[08:02] Maya: we can run it for you or provide instructions and the script. For fairness we usually run both: you run one replay copy and we run from our infra, then compare metrics.
[08:12] Samir: fine. about benchmarks: what metrics exactly will be in the final report?
[08:16] Alejandro: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, tail latency heatmaps, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, queue depths, batch sizes, error rates, cost estimate per 1M tokens, and recommended config with expected cost/latency curve.
[08:33] Priya: ok. timeline recap?
[08:36] Maya: propose:
 - Week 0 (this week): share capture tool & benchmark template (Redwood) and Nexus provides 48h sanitized capture by 2026-12-03.
 - Week 1 (2026-12-04 to 12-10): Redwood runs baseline hosted + dedicated replay tests; run burst ladder.
 - Week 2 (2026-12-11 to 12-17): tuning, re-run specific scenarios, finalize report.
 - Deliverable: final report + recommended config + slide deck by 2026-12-18.
[09:05] Priya: that fits our internal timeline. we have a compliance gate 12-20, so report by 12-18 is good.
[09:12] Lola: please send SOC2 and SSO docs earlier.
[09:15] Maya: will do today.
[09:17] Samir: one more operational question: how do you handle KV cache invalidation when model versions change?
[09:23] Alejandro: we tag KV by model-version and prompt-hash; during rollouts we have an auto-regen policy or warmup mode. We'll show options in the tuning phase.
[09:33] Priya: examples of failure modes we worry about: token explosion in certain user workflows. can you detect and throttle?
[09:40] Alejandro: yes we can add per-route token caps and circuit-breakers; those will show up in the tuning pass.
[09:46] Maya: ok wrapping up — to confirm next steps: Samir will upload capture by 12-03, Redwood (Alejandro) will share baseline harness and run initial tests week of 12-04, Maya will send SOC2 and pricing sketch by 12-01.
[09:59] Priya: correct. also please include a short checklist for onboarding private/KMS options.
[10:04] Maya: will include.
[10:06] Lola: thanks everyone.
[10:08] Alejandro: thanks, we'll follow up in email with the schedule and links to the repo.
[10:12] Maya: thanks all, talk soon.
